source.title: Source
source.note: The image is processed locally, in the browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.

mixer.title: Channel mixer
mixer.note: The matrix has no colour: these weights decide how much of each channel goes into the luminance. It is the coloured filter of black and white photography — raising the red lightens skin and darkens a blue sky.

led.title: LED output
led.note: At 2 steps the render goes binary and the dithering does all the work. Past ~16 steps the matrix renders real greys and the dither only serves to break up banding in gradients.

exportCard.title: Export
exportCard.note1: The .json is a drawing in the
exportCard.note2: format — one frame, {leds} LED instructions. It also carries this page's settings, under a key other readers ignore: the same file opens over there and reloads here with all its sliders.

glyphlapse.description: Preview of the GlyphLapse Glyph Toy: time passing, broken down on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).
glyphlapse.onlyOne: Only one lapse enabled — the toy has nowhere to switch to

lapse.title: Displayed lapse
lapse.note1: A long press on the Glyph Button moves to the next enabled lapse. Lapse I cannot be disabled: a toy with no active lapse would have nothing to show.
lapse.note2: The selected tab is the one the toy displays: there is no lapse you configure on one side and another that runs on the other. That is how the settings app behaves — picking a tab switches the toy.

deadline.title: Deadline
deadline.note: A deadline still ahead flips the toy into a countdown. On crossing it, it plays a four-second arrival — In 10 s is there to see it without waiting.

format.title: Format
format.note1: Dense writes the whole granularity, two units per line when it has to. Compact keeps only the two leading units, in 5×7. Cycle scrolls them one by one. Days gives the total alone.
format.note2: Leading units at zero are dropped: “0Y 0M 3D” would waste two lines of the disc saying that nothing has happened.

seconds.title: Seconds
seconds.note1: Ring fills the rim from twelve o'clock — clockwise when time accumulates, anticlockwise when it runs out. Hourglass raises or lowers a level of sand whose surface is a cone: tip at the centre in “since”, funnel in “until”.
seconds.note2: The height of the sand is found by bisection rather than computed: the area of a disc above a line has no simple expression, and fourteen iterations are enough to land on the right amount to within a cell.

readout.title: Readout
readout.note: The breakdown follows the calendar, not a division: two months are 59, 60 or 62 days depending on which. It is the same count as Period.between on the toy side.

glyphslot.description: Preview of the GlyphSlot Glyph Toy: a slot machine on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).

status.idle: Long-press the Glyph Button to spin

spinCard.title: Spin
spinCard.note1: The two forcing buttons do not exist on the toy: they are here to see the effects without waiting. A jackpot lands at 5 %, a plain win at 15 % — checking that a seven-second animation reads well by rolling for it is no way to work.
spinCard.note2: On the device the only control is a long press on the Glyph Button. Holding the one in the photo for 450 ms does the same thing.

roll.title: Last spin
roll.note: The payline is the central seven-row window. Neighbouring symbols stay lit at a fifth of the intensity: that is what makes it read as a window onto a spinning band rather than three independent cells.

reels.title: Reels
reels.note1: A reel is not a symbol drawn at the finish: it is a continuous band of five symbols that spins, and stopping it means choosing where to brake. So the neighbours of the winning symbol go past before it settles.
reels.note2: The order of the symbols differs from one reel to the next — reel i advances by i+1 modulo 5. The neighbours of an aligned symbol are not the same on all three, and an alignment cannot be read in advance from what goes past above it.
reels.note3: On the spin, the reel first backs up slowly — a spring being wound — then releases. Without that recoil the start is a uniform glide that does not say anything was pulled.
reels.note4: The braking distance is drawn from a range rather than computed to the shortest: braking over the minimum distance would stop the reel almost immediately whenever the target is already close, and the machine would be seen aiming.

fx.title: Effects
fx.note1: A plain win pulses the rim ring. The jackpot takes the screen for seven and a half seconds: triple strobe, concentric shock waves, a scrolling JACKPOT banner, fireworks with gravity, then a zooming 7.
fx.note2: The shake offsets the frame by a whole cell. The original preview shook the canvas: a Glyph Matrix has its LEDs soldered on, it cannot move by half a pixel — and a transformed canvas would leave the grid of physical pixels the whole preview alignment rests on.

reject.tooEarly: The die has only just left
reject.tooLate: The die is landing — let it settle
reject.inAir: The die is in the air

status.rest: The die is at rest — shake to throw
status.tumble: It tumbles — a shake throws it again

throwCard.title: Throw
throwCard.forceNote: These buttons do not exist on the toy: they are here to see a given face without waiting for it. The value is drawn at the start anyway — the animation does not discover it, it leads to it.
throwCard.deviceNote: On the device: shaking the phone throws the die, a long press on the Glyph Button changes solid — which is what the first two buttons above do.
throwCard.expected: At {throws, plural, one {# throw} other {# throws}}, each face expects {each} — the dotted line.

timing.title: Timing
timing.note1: The red band is the window where a shake throws the die again — before it, the previous gesture is still ending; after it, the die is choosing its face.
timing.note2: Six bounces, then the camera moves in to reveal the top face.

render.title: The render
render.note1: On twenty-five LEDs a side, a die seen three-quarters on does not read: the resting pose is the close-up from directly above, and three-quarter views only exist in flight.
render.note2: A pip is 3 × 3 cells, a number is a stretched glyph, and the mark is only printed at the close-up — in flight it would be cut by an edge and change on every bounce.

sonoglyph.description: Preview of the two Sonoglyph Glyph Toys: spectrum visualiser and needle VU meter, on the Glyph Matrix of the Nothing Phone (3).
sonoglyph.sub: Two Glyph Toys that read the sound level

voice.name: Voice
voice.note: 200 Hz – 4 kHz band, ~4 Hz syllabic modulation

music.name: Music
music.note: 2 Hz pulse, marked bass and short highs

toyCard.note1: The project was abandoned and archived for technical reasons, but the code is still readable

shown.title: Displayed toy
shown.spectrum1: One band per column, 40 Hz to 16 kHz in third-octave steps, already A-weighted — without which the bass crushes the twenty-two columns above it. Rendered all or nothing: a LED is on or off, no shades.
shown.spectrum2: Height alone carries the level. The centre axis stays lit at all times, it is the baseline — and at low level the only visible thing.
shown.needle: The dial is the outline of the disc over ± 90°, so the whole upper half; the pivot is at the exact centre. Major graduations: {ticks} dB(A). A single needle, on the Fast level. The number below is 5×7, rounded to the integer.

source.title: Source
source.note: Neither computes a level: they produce samples, and it is the toy's chain — A-weighting, Fast detector, band bank — that turns them into a dB. The mic goes through an AudioWorklet, with AGC, noise reduction and echo cancellation switched off. Nothing leaves the browser.

sim.title: Simulated signal
sim.note: The setting is in dB(A) and not dBFS: the gain makes up for what the weighting will take off the chosen timbre, measured when the timbre changes. Without that compensation the slider would lie by 9 dB between the sine and the traffic.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.note: This figure is not measured. 120 dB is the order of magnitude of a phone MEMS, whose full scale falls around there. Until the unit is characterised, the displayed level is only right to within ±5 dB — the toys are indicators, not sound level meters. The slider is here to see what calibration moves; on the device it is a constant.
